images.caption:
Guests at the Police Ball and wedding at Cloncurry, Queensland, 1938.
Police Ball in a decorated hall at Cloncurry in 1938. Inspector Howard is the tall man standing on the left wearing spectacles. Snr. Sergeant Sproule, second man from the right, is standing behing the large drum. A wedding party is seated in the photograph. From left to right they are: the bridesmaid, Jean White; bridegroom, Constable Jim Williams; bride, (nee) Norma Rose; bestman, Jack Connelly. All are wearing formal evening wear (Description supplied with the photograph).

images.filename: StateLibQld 1 136647 Debutantes at the Cloncurry Coronation Debutante Ball.jpg
images.caption:
Debutantes at the Cloncurry Coronation Debutante Ball
Debutante Merle Hartig being presented to the Shire Chairman Nobby Clark. Matron of Honour, Mrs Ede Lemmon makes the introduction (Description supplied with photograph.) Cloncurry started with the discovery of copper. It is situated in the west of Queensland at the junction roads from Townsville, the Gulf of Carpentaria, Longreach, Mount Isa and Winton. First Qantas flight landed in Cloncurry and John Flynn (Flynn of the Inland) established the Flying Doctor service here.

images.filename: StateLibQld 1 161285 Taylor family and railway officials at Fort Constantine Station, Queensland, 1911.jpg
images.caption:
Taylor family and railway officials at Fort Constantine Station, Queensland, 1911
Group photograph of the Commissioner, Chief Engineer, and the Taylor Family at Fort Constantine Station. This shot was taken in November, 1911, during the Commissioner's inspection of country from Cloncurry to King's Hole in connection with a proposed rail line from Cloncurry to Mt. Cuthbert. The Commissioner was also inspecting the route of the Great Western Railway from Winton to the Diamantina River. The Commissioner and another man, possibly the Chief Engineer, are both wearing white pith helmets. The commissioner is seated on a folding chair.
